completion_guardrail: Child tickets and merged PRs are progress evidence, not goal completion evidence by themselves.

summary.reason: The release ledger has strong validation coverage, but the full release assembly path is still distributed across release cadence documentation, CI workflows, and individual generator/check scripts. A single operator-facing assembly receipt or runner is still needed before #344 can be closed.

criteria.goal_acceptance: Release assembly has one documented, deterministic path that regenerates and checks registry, schema, report, shard, compatibility, impact, and evidence artifacts.

evidence.finding: Documents draft, verify, recommended evidence regeneration, schema sync, manifest sync, and ledger ownership checks.
CI checks policy artifacts, release verify/readiness, shard archive evidence, release zip packaging, and shard consistency.
Manual workflow can verify or draft a selected manifest and produce release zip plus optional shard archive evidence.

criteria.gap: The path is not yet a single checked-in operator command or receipt that proves all generation/check steps were run in order from the current checkout.
criteria.next_action: Create a bounded child ticket to consolidate release assembly into an operator-facing runner or receipt.

criteria.goal_acceptance: CI gates cover the same invariants that a release operator depends on locally; no manifest-bound artifact requires hand-maintained bytes, sha256, schema URI, or derived report metadata.

evidence.finding: CI runs schema sync check, manifest sync check, release-ledger ownership validation, report validators, source runtime checks, impact checks, and consumer compatibility checks.
Owns schema index and schema artifact digest synchronization.
Owns non-schema manifest artifact bytes and sha256 synchronization.
Maps every manifest artifact kind to owner, generator, checker, package relationship, schema relationship, and exemption boundary.

criteria.gap: CI and local commands are aligned for current validators, but the repo still lacks a single local release assembly receipt that records the exact operator run and command outcomes.
criteria.next_action: Carry this into the release assembly receipt child instead of closing #344.

criteria.goal_acceptance: The manifest, schema index, source report inventory, release package, shard package, and consumer compatibility report are mutually consistent and independently checkable.

evidence.finding: Contains 70 manifest-bound artifacts across 27 artifact kinds, including 44 schema artifacts.
Indexes 44 schema contracts and checks schema artifact bytes and sha256.
Inventories 151 source-scoped reports and confirms all 26 schema-backed reports are schema-indexed.
Binds source contracts, source runtime evidence, error/action routing, downstream impact, source reference drift, and source report inventory as manifest evidence contracts.
Checks release zip entries and optional shard archive source registry identity against the selected manifest.
Packages and checks registry shard archives from a generated shard inventory.

criteria.next_action: Keep existing checks in CI and release cadence.

criteria.goal_acceptance: Source runtime evidence and report inventories make source-level readiness auditable without listing every nested report in the top-level manifest.

evidence.finding: Summarizes five sources, 4774 evidence items, 12 blockers, 8 warnings, and four sources without runtime evidence.
Records source-scoped report paths, bytes, sha256, schema URIs, and schema-index status without requiring every nested report in the top-level manifest.
Validates source runtime rollup data and generated markdown readiness view.
Validates source report inventory coverage and schema-index linkage.

criteria.next_action: Keep expanding source runtime evidence through separate runtime evidence tickets; do not block this ledger-audit criterion on full provider coverage.

criteria.goal_acceptance: Downstream impact and consumer compatibility are connected to release evidence strongly enough to answer whether a release is safe to consume, blocked, or needs manual review.

evidence.finding: Records five release changes, target-specific actions, and two manual-review changes, with release evidence inputs for error/action routing and source report inventory.
Reports seven consumers, two proven consumers, one blocked consumer, canonical registry requirement, optional shard assets, and runtime manual-review evidence.
Validates registry impact rollup inputs and the downstream impact contract in consumer compatibility evidence.
Fails if source runtime blockers remain but runtime manual-review evidence, error/action routing evidence, or downstream manual-review impact evidence disappears.

criteria.next_action: Keep compatibility evidence current whenever source runtime blockers or downstream contracts change.

criteria.goal_acceptance: A requirement-by-requirement completion audit proves the above from current files, commands, CI state, and linked PR evidence.

evidence.finding: This audit maps every #344 acceptance criterion to evidence, verdict, gap, and next action.
Validates the audit structure, evidence paths, criteria coverage, and the rule that a non-complete goal must keep follow-up work.

criteria.next_action: Use this audit to keep #344 open until the release assembly gap is closed and re-audited.

follow_up_children.title: Consolidate release ledger assembly receipt
follow_up_children.reason: Close the remaining deterministic release assembly gap by producing one operator-facing command or receipt that records the full generation/check sequence and outcomes from the current checkout.
